entities.name: Dominaria Remastered
entities.description:
Dominaria Remastered is the second remastered Magic: The Gathering set to appear in paper. It was released on January 13, 2023.

Dominaria Remastered reaches across Magic's sets to bring together a mix of the familiar and nostalgic cards representing the breadth of Dominaria's history, from the earliest sets through the modern day. It is a fully draftable set featuring cards from 27 sets that took place on Dominaria. Note that Tempest, Stronghold, Exodus, and Nemesis took place on the plane of Rath, which would later be overlaid onto Dominaria, but R&D chose not to include them because they didn't take place on Dominaria at the time and the first three had already been used in Tempest Remastered.

The 27 sets are: Alpha, Antiquities, Legends, The Dark, Fallen Empires, Ice Age, Alliances, Coldsnap, Mirage, Visions, Urza's Saga, Urza's Legacy, Urza's Destiny, Prophecy, Invasion, Planeshift, Apocalypse, Odyssey, Torment, Judgement, Onslaught, Legions, Scourge, Time Spiral, Planar Chaos, Future Sight and Dominaria. There are also three cards that first appeared in Modern Horizons.

Dominaria Remastered features 261 regular cards , and includes randomly inserted premium versions of all cards. #262-401 are retro frame versions of a selection of the previous cards, #402-411 are retro frame basic lands, #412-456 are a selection of borderless versions. #457 is the release card.
entities.short_description: Dominaria Remastered is the second remastered Magic: The Gathering set to appear in paper. It was released on January 13, 2023.

entities.name: Dueling Chasm of Golthonor
entities.description:
The Dueling Chasm of Golthonor is an immense canyon located on Dominaria's continent of Corondor.

The Chasm was formed from the explosion of power that was released when Dakkon Blackblade used the Black Blade to slay the Elder Dragon Piru after Geyadrone Dihada summoned her and Chromium Rhuell to fight him for her (though it was really all a ruse to get Dakkon to kill one of the dragons so that she could absorb the power from a dragon's soul). It was located in the Rift of Golthonor just east of the Spine.

Later, in the year 1281 by the Reckoning of the Sages of Minorad, it was where Jared Carthalion, Kristina of the Woods, Altair of Coloni, and Caliphear the Nightmare had a battle against Ravidel. Jared destroyed the various monoliths in the canyon with a powerful spell during the battle. From here, Ravidel launched his Mox Beacon, spreading his evil, and then disappeared in the chaos of the crumbling monoliths of the chasm; Jared ascended and became a planeswalker in time to planeswalk away from the crumbling monoliths and save Kristina from falling or being crushed, though Altair was killed.

entities.name: Ekundu Mountains
entities.description:
The Ekundu Mountains are the highest mountain range in Jamuraa on Dominaria.

The Ekundu Mountains are a barrier between Suq’Ata in the north, Femeref in the south, the Mwonvuli Jungle in the west and the Great Desert in the east. The Ekundu Mountains are home to many dwarves and griffins.

The vast mountain chain branches off into five other ranges. In the north-west it branches of into the Talruum Mountains, in the south-west into the Teremko Mountains. The small range of the mineral-rich Kitu Mountains branches of from the central south of the Ekundu. In the south-east the Ekundu branches into the Jotoka Mountains which were mined as well. The name of the final branch, which extends to the north-east, is unknown.

During the early years of Femeref, Suq’Ata marched against the dwarven denizens of Ekundu and forced them southwards into the Femeref town of Terorq.
entities.short_description: The Ekundu Mountains are the highest mountain range in Jamuraa on Dominaria.

entities.name: Elder Dragons
entities.description:
The comic Elder Dragons, based on the cycle of Elder Dragons from the Magic card set Legends was published by Armada in two parts. The first volume was released in April, 1996 and the second in May of that year.

! Title !! Author !! Publishing date !! Set !! Setting (plane) !! Featuring

The warlord Red Donald and his daughter Ad'Amra arrive in the town of Mors Ridge, where a boy called Ham performs "Tickery" magic to keep the Elder Dragon Palladia-Mors at bay. Donald doesn't believe the story and when a magical storm picks up his Dragon Whelp familiar convinces him to start digging canals in the ridge. This actually awakens Palladia-Mors. Then, the dragon whelp is revealed to be her cousin Vaevictis Asmadi. He had manipulated Donald in order to awaken Palladia, needing her to lift the curse that had turned him into a whelp. Palladia does so, and together with an army of zombies and orcs the two Elders start wreaking havoc, killing Red Donald.

Throughout the chaos Ham has been acting strangely. He refuses to hurt Palladia, and pushes away Ad’Amra, who has fallen in love with him. In the end it is revealed that Ham is actually the benevolent Elder Dragon Chromium Rhuell. Chromium convinces Vaevictis to turn on Palladia, but Palladia reverses one of Vaevictis' spells, and he disappears from the battle. Finally, Ad’Amra and Chromium manage to put the sleep-spell back on Palladia.

entities.name: Eln Forest
entities.description:
Eln Forest was a forest in northwestern Terisiare during the Dark Age of Dominaria.

It was located near the edge of the Colekgan Mountains, across a wide flat plain from the Urhaalan Valley. Eln Forest was populated by Ironroot treefolk, and a tribe of elves that came into conflict with the Urhaalan minotaurs through the schemes of the sorceress Sacumon.

During the onset of the Ice Age, Eln Forest was slowly covered and destroyed by the widening Great Glacier.
entities.short_description: Eln Forest was a forest in northwestern Terisiare during the Dark Age of Dominaria.

entities.name: Endless Sea
entities.description:
The Endless Sea is a body of water off the northern Terisian Isles

The Endless Sea is the part of the Dominarian ocean that lies north of the Terisian Isles (former Terisiare). The Endless Sea borders the northern shores of Gulmany, specifically Efuan Pincar, and onto the shores of the Balduvian Steppes. It connects to the Ilesemare Sea in the west, the Sea of Laments in the south, and the Videnthian Sea in the east.

The Endless Sea bordered the northern coasts of Terisiare before that continent was split into smaller islands. During the Brothers' War, the sea ran along from the Colekgan Mountains, past Ronom Glacier to the Malpiri Plains. During the Dark Age, the Endless Sea started forming icebergs, and whole sheets of ice formed in the northernmost parts. During the Ice Age, the ice floes coalesced into massive ice caps, with glacial spurs running onto the continent itself.

entities.name: Fall of Storgard
entities.description:
The Fall of Storgard was an event that occurred during the Ice Age on Dominaria.

Following the corruption of king Miko by the planeswalker Tevesh Szat, the council of Storgard had opted to stay in the city even in the face of the encroaching Raynor Glacier. Opposing this decision was Oriel Kjeldos, Jason Carthalion, Hurn, and Mariska, and the outcome of the decision to stay was put to a duel between Jason and the mage Freyalise (before her ascension as a planeswalker).

Jason won the duel, allowing those who wanted to leave the city, while the rest stayed behind. The refugees eventually settled further south and east on the ruined foundations of old Penregon, which ironically had met the same fate as Storgard millennia before. Here, they founded the city of Kjeld, which would become the capital of the nation of Kjeldor. Those who stayed behind in Storgard were eventually swallowed by the glacier, wiping them all out, much to Tevesh Szat's pleasure.
entities.short_description: The Fall of Storgard was an event that occurred during the Ice Age on Dominaria.

entities.name: Lim-Dûl's Battle
entities.description:
Lim-Dûl's Battle was an event that occurred during the last part of the Ice Age on Dominaria.

The battle happened at the mouth of one of the main passes through the Karplusan Mountains, north of Krov. The Balduvians led by Lovisa Coldeyes and the Kjeldorans led by General Varchild set up camp there, waiting for Lim-Dûl to arrive. Several mages participated in the battle, including the archmage Jodah, the taskmage Jaya Ballard, the royal mage Gustha Ebbasdotter, and the necromancer Lim-Dûl himself.

The battle was fierce, and Lim-Dûl's forces had the superior number. After exhausting her spells on a warded Avram Garrisson, Gustha Ebbasdotter was swarmed by piles of undead, and she barely had time to scream before falling. Jaya faced off against her former friend turned zombie, the skyknight Belenda Danisdotter. After hesitating, Jaya managed to kill Belenda. Jodah summoned the Lost Order of Jarkeld to join the battle to protect Lovisa Coldeyes, whose barbarians had surged too far ahead.

The Keeper of Tresserhorn, Chaeska, was also present, and he wielded the sword arm of the dismantled Márton Stromgald. He faced off against Jaya, wearing a red ward to protect himself against her fire spells, but she used blue mana and cast Unsummon on him, returning him directly to the halls to Tresserhorn.
entities.short_description: Lim-Dûl's Battle was an event that occurred during the last part of the Ice Age on Dominaria.

entities.name: Excerpts from The Antiquities War
entities.description:
Excerpts from The Antiquities War, by Kayla bin-Kroog: A New Translation and Commentary is a two-volume work by Taysir of Rabiah. It is a translation of the fourth and fifth volumes of The Antiquities War.

It is my purpose to provide a contemporary version of The Antiquities War, a classic in Argivian literature. Although "The Story of Urza and Mishra" is well-known throughout Terisiare, a modern interpretation was overdue. The text speaks for itself. I shall therefore confine my expository comments to footnotes.

"The Story of Urza and Mishra" takes place thousands of years after the fall of the mysterious Thran Empire. Some say that the Thran discovered a source of great power, but they were not ready to use this power properly-- and it destroyed them.

During the time of Urza and Mishra, Fallaji nomads routinely searched for Thran artifacts in the Western Desert. With caravans filled with bits and pieces of the past, the Fallaji traveled east-- to the edge of the desert, where they traded with various city-states and schools specializing in the study of Thran antiquities.

Fallen Angel is a Magic: The Gathering comic published by ARMADA in May 1996.

! Title !! Author !! Publishing date !! Set !! Setting (plane) !! Featuring

The warlord Mandek Ironfist gets the wizard Xarl to turn a summoned Serra Angel into a fallen angel with an artifact called the Horned Halo. The angel, Trine, turns into an unstoppable killing machine and Mandek creates an empire. Three centuries later Mandek is long gone, but Xarl is still around, dominating the continent of Corondor thanks to Trine. He appoints his spellsquire Eskil as his heir. ! Title !! Author !! Publishing date !! Set !! Setting (plane) !! Featuring

The story begins in a Dwarven fortress somewhere in the Crimson Peaks in the year 170 AR. The dwarf Kaylen and human Tymolin Loneglade are struggling to hold back wave after wave of invading Orcs and Goblins. Sneaking behind Kaylen an orc runs him through from behind before Tymolin can warn him. Avenging Kaylen Tymolin slays the Orc, but Kaylen is already lying dead on the ground. Banished by a Dwarven leader she heads to Havenwood to seek her brother Tev.

Meanwhile, in the town of Montford an ex-Icatian Priest Oliver Farrel is whipping up a frenzy charging that the Order of the Ebon Hand is amongst them, and that Tymoiln herself is the dark God Tourach. Farrel then appoints Sianna to be his champion bestowing Farrel's Mantle upon her. As his concubine and champion her first charge is to track down and slay Tymolin. This being unbeknownst to her, Tymolin tries to persuade Tev to travel with her Montford to warn them of the invading Orc-Goblin army.

entities.name: Feldon's Cane
entities.description:
Feldon's Cane was an artifact found by Feldon in the Ronom Glacier.

Its origins are mysterious, as it was specifically not of Thran design, nor dwarven or goblin origin. The mysteries of the cane led Feldon to travel to Terisia City in search of any information on it, but the extensive library had nothing to match the runes on the cane's shaft. His presence there then led to his part in the Union of the Third Path, and it was also what brought him into contact with his future wife, Loran - so in that sense, the cane brought Feldon luck and happiness for a time.

Feldon was lame in one leg and used the cane as a walking stick.

Many years later, after Loran's death, Feldon sought magic to resurrect her. He approached a necromancer in the swamps north of Ronom Lake. The necromancer agreed to bring Loran back from the dead for a price - and that price was Feldon's Cane. Feldon reluctantly agreed to this and gave his cane to the necromancer. When Feldon awoke the following morning, the necromancer and all his hollow-eyed guards had disappeared. That is the last known information on the strange artifact, whose runic secrets may remain forever unknown.

entities.name: Femeref
entities.description:
Femeref is a strong religious state in Jamuraa on Dominaria.

Centuries ago, when the land was ruled entirely by Zhalfir, an internal religious dispute led the church to secede. They had objections to the Shadow Creed's treatment of the dead. The church created its own province called Femeref after the Zhalfirin word fethe, meaning "judgment." The fledgling nation was ruled by a grand assembly known as the Council of Voices. In time, Femeref grew apart from Zhalfir, aided by the discovery of rich gold deposits. Eventually, tales of the mineral wealth within Femeref's deep mountains spread to the Suq'Ata Empire. The empire annexed the lands bordering Zhalfir and began to mine the mountains, pushing the dwarven residents into Femeref. The leaders of Femeref happily accepted the new refugees, as their skills would increase Femeref's gold yield substantially.

The land of Zhalfir was phased out by Teferi Planeswalker during the Phyrexian Invasion. Four hundred years after, when the temporal crisis threatened to destroy the Multiverse, the Zhalfirin time rift was sealed by Jeska without Teferi's guidance and the necessary synchronization with Zhalfir's return, causing the land to be (probably) forever doomed to non-existence out of time and space. The Femeref nation is thus the only heir and bearer of the legacy of the five-millennium old civilization and nation.

As of 4562, Femeref was ruled by a magistrate, Sidar Teshunda, who was advised by the ten-member Council of Voices in the Great Chamber. Council members include Councilor Gbega, Councilor Jabras, and Historian Awateh. When Femeref was threatened by a Phyrexian Colossus, it fell into infighting and paranoia. It was only Esteemed Speaker Niambi who was able to convince Teshunda to grant the Efravans refuge.

entities.name: Fountain of Youth
entities.description:
The Fountain of Youth was an artifact that imbued immortality to those who drank it.

The Fountain of Youth was situated in the middle of the city square of Pitdown, though none save the pigeons knew its secret.. The fountain had lions' head statues that poured the water into the basin and had once held a grand look, but it was poorly tended, and the waters were covered with dirt, algae, and various weeds. During the Battle of Pitdown, Jodah happened upon the fountain as he was seeking refuge from the fighting. He had to hide beneath the waters to avoid being seen by a band of goblin raiders, and accidentally swallowed some of the disgusting water. While he did notice that his leg wound had healed afterward, he did not ascribe this to the fountain at the time. It was only years later, when he realized he was not aging like others were, that he understood what had happened.

entities.description:
Gerrard's Quest was a comic series published by Dark Horse Comics in March - June 1998. The series was written by one of the industry's top writers, Mike Grell, and featured artwork by acclaimed artists Pop Mahn and Mark Harrison. The series followed the Weatherlight Saga.

! Title !! Author !! Publishing date !! Set !! Setting (plane) !! Featuring

Gerrard has been given a Legacy of tremendous power, but it has been scattered, and his captain, has been captured by the forces of Volrath, lord of the plane of Rath. Though Gerrard has no desire to seek out the Legacy and assume responsibility for its wise use, he now has the obligation to rescue his friend. But Gerrard and the crew of the flying ship Weatherlight have no idea of what dangers they'll face upon their arrival in Rath!

High above the Plains of Rath, Gerrard and the crew of the flying ship Weatherlight are attacked by the awesome power of Volrath's battleship, the Predator. Volrath's forces, led by the fierce Greven il-Vec, board the Weatherlight in an attempt to steal Gerrard's mysterious legacy. Gerrard and Greven come face to face in gruesome combat as the crew of the Weatherlight fight for their lives!

entities.name: Golden Argosy
entities.description:
The Golden Argosy was a legendary Keldon longship that was perched atop the Keldon Necropolis on Dominaria.

It was prophesied that at the coming of the Keldon Twilight, Golden Argosy would transport the risen champions of Keld to the final battlefield. However, when the Twilight actually took place, Golden Argosy instead rescued the living Keldon warriors from the freezing waters that had engulfed the battlefield, as well as the Skyshroud elves that had been aiding them. It then transported them to Urborg, where the most crucial battle of the Phyrexian Invasion was taking place. The vessel traveled impossibly fast to Urborg and, upon disembarking, the passengers' memories of the journey faded like it was a dream. Having fulfilled its destiny, Golden Argosy departed and for a long time was not seen again.

Fulfilling a second twilight, the Golden Argosy reappeared with warriors, including the legendary Astor, to help fight during the second Phyrexian invasion. It participated in the Battle of the Mana Rig.

entities.name: Golgothian Sylex
entities.description:
The Golgothian Sylex (also known as the Argivian Sylex) was a massively destructive artifact created by the Thran or an earlier civilization. Urza used it to unleash the Sylex Blast and end the Brothers' War.

The Sylex was accidentally netted by Yumok fishermen in 36 AR, and sent to Feldon in Terisia City for study. It was made of an unknown copper-like metal, roughly one foot in diameter, and described as a cross between a bowl mounted on a thick pedestal and a squat, wide-rimmed goblet. Its interior was carved with glyphs in several languages, including Thran, Fallaji, and Sumifan, making it a Rosetta Stone for the others.

Those glyphs named the item "sylex" and its origin "Golgoth". Feldon could not determine whether Golgoth was a location or a person responsible for the item's creation without sufficient context. He translated the Fallaji glyphs as:

A counterfeit Sylex named Ashnod's Cylix was said to have been created by Ashnod from the hollowed-out skull of the Qadir of the Fallaji Empire, whom she killed during the Fall of Kroog.. In truth, she had created it by more traditional means - coppersmithing. This cylix was used to fool the Brotherhood of Gix, who craved the real Sylex, even as Mishra himself refused it.

entities.name: Halquina Mountains
entities.description:
The Halquina Mountains were a large mountainous region in southwestern Terisiare on Dominaria.

Halquina formed the southern province of Almaaz and contrasted with the more northerly province of Sumifa. Halquina was a mountainous region with an arid climate, though not without trees.

The Halquina mountains lasted past the Brothers' War and through the Dark Age, but when the Ice Age started, they were buried under the Great Glacier. When the ice retreated after thousands year years, the mountains had been ground into the sea, and only some of the taller peaks remained as a set of islands south and west of the main island of Almaaz. One of these islands features Sarraza and the River Kingdom.

entities.name: Hand of Righteous Retribution
entities.description:
The Hand of Righteous Retribution, also known as The Twice-Drawn Sword is a powerful magical sword on Dominaria. About a foot wide and inscribed with powerful runes, the sword is not meant to be used for its' blade, but to channel powerful magical energy.

The sword belonged to Captain Hask, who used it to injure, but not kill, the dragon that claimed to be Zumaki of the Bottomless Pool. It was then taken by Tania Cayce, who used it to kill the beast and the skeletal remains of the real Zumaki. Supposedly this would be enough to permanently kill the dragon, but after Tania and Hask had left, and the Hand of Righteous Retribution lost amidst the rubble of the dragon's lair, the creature regenerated still.

According to myths, the Hand was blessed by both the High Primate of Angelfire and the Serran Mother Superior. This is a bold claim, as the Church of Angelfire has long opposed the Serrans. The myth also claims that the sword can only be drawn twice. Once in anger and once in wisdom. According to the myth: "outrage is the true spark that becomes the fire of retribution, but wisdom is the only path to true justice".

According to the Pixie Vaan though, anyone can use the sword, as long as they allow its enchanted energy to build up between uses. He claims the myth is but an ancient ruse by priests and generals to prevent the wielder of the Hand to run rampant.

entities.name: Ice Age
entities.description:
The Ice Age, also known as the Time of Ice and the Time of the Eternal Snows, was a period of extreme cold in Dominaria lasting from 450 AR to 2934 AR. It was initiated by the Sylex Blast at the end of the Brothers' War, and prolonged by the magic of the planeswalkers Leshrac and Tevesh Szat, until Freyalise cast her World Spell to end it.

The Ice Age lasted depending on where one places its beginning over two thousand years. It is a period that, save for its very end, is largely lost in Dominaria's historical record. As a result of the period's opaqueness to historians, most on the plane assume that it was a quiet period. In reality, it saw the birth of the modern nations of Terisiare and the refinement of magic into its present state. It was a time when planeswalkers held sway over the world, when great beasts evolved to battle the cold, and when mages sought out the greatest secrets of their arts.

The Ice Age generally referred to in history is the one from the time of the kingdom of Storgard until the casting of the World Spell. The age following is known as The Thaw.

entities.name: Ice Cauldron
entities.description:
The Ice Cauldron was an artifact from Dominaria, capable of storing mass amounts of mana.

During the casting of the World Spell, the Ice Cauldron was situated at the bottom-most part of the crater, directly beneath Freyalise’s floating form. It was a huge metallic bowl, a cauldron of frosted iron. Rime formed around the outside of the cauldron despite the warmth of the surroundings. The interior of the cauldron was inscribed with runes, spiraling into the center of the pot. At the bottom of the cauldron was Jodah's Mirror, placed at the center of the ritual. The bowl was a duplication of the Golgothian Sylex, made by Freyalise based on original notes that had been preserved in the School of the Unseen. The Ice Cauldron was thus used to end Dominaria’s Ice Age, and much of the destruction it would have caused was alleviated by Jodah channeling the heat of the spell through the safe havens, destroying them in the process. It is unknown if the cauldron itself survived this process.

entities.name: Ilesemare Sea
entities.description:
The Ilesemare Sea is a body of water off the western Terisian Isles

The Ilesemare Sea is the part of the Dominarian ocean that lies west of the Terisian Isles (former Terisiare). The Ilesemare Sea borders the western shores of Lat-Nam in the south and Gulmany in the north. It connects to the Lat-Nam Straits in the south, the Sea of Almaaz in the southeast, and the Endless Sea in the northeast.

The Ilesemare Sea bordered the western coasts of Terisiare before that continent was split into smaller islands. During the Brothers' War, the sea ran along the south shores of the Colekgan Mountains. During the Dark Age, the Ilesemare Sea bordered Urhaalan Valley, Eln Forest, Shingol, Iwset and Jehesic, and during the Ice Age, it ran along the Great Glacier and western Lat-Nam.

entities.name: Iwset
entities.description:
Iwset was a city-state during the Dark Age, located on the western coast of Terisiare near the Lat-Nam Straits, bordering the Ilesemare Sea.

At a certain point during the Dark Age, Iwset was ruled by Lord Peemel, with the advisors Digody and Apepei counseling him. Iwset lay south across the Lat-Nam Straits from Jehesic, not far from Desolation Point, and the Iwsetians had long been in a tense rivalry with their neighbor. After the Iwset-Jehesic War, Iwset was ruled by Edara and Apepei, although with neither the sigil of the city nor the true heir at their disposal.

entities.name: Jalum Tome
entities.description:
The Jalum Tome was a powerful, ancient book of Thran civilization containing all their knowledge and designs. Urza used it as a construction manual for many artifacts that he created, including the Weatherlight.

The Jalum Tome was a Thran artifact that surfaced as part of the dowry for Princess Kayla bin-Kroog. It was this artifact that inspired Urza to participate in the contest to move the Warlord of Kroog's statue, using his smarts rather than brawn.

The Jalum Tome stayed in the possession of Urza's family after his marriage, and at times, Kayla felt he was more interested in the book than in her. The Jalum Tome eventually passed into the possession of their grandson, Jarsyl, who took it with him to the Conclave of Mages.

At some point after joining the Conclave, Jarsyl discovered a portal to Phyrexia, possibly the one at Koilos. What happened to the Jalum Tome after that is unknown. Urza recovered it at some point as part of his work on the Legacy, and it passed into Karn's hands.

The Jester's Cap was an artifact from Dominaria, that enables the wielder to discover their foes’ strengths as well as their weaknesses.

Lim-Dûl possessed it when he arrived on Shandalar. In the Catacombs, he used it to discover what Bani Bakur and Ravash Mog feared, leading to Ravash Mog's death.

entities.name: Jodah's Mirror
entities.description:
Jodah's Mirror was a powerful artifact in the possession of the archmage Jodah during Dominaria's Dark Age and Ice Age. During his apprenticeship, this Reflecting Mirror was given to him by the wandering mage Voska.

According to Voska, the mirror's origins predate the Brothers' War, indicating it may be of Thran origin. Voska's teacher found it in an abandoned war machine pitched into one Ashnod's slave pits in the Great Desert after the Sylex Blast. Voska then received it from his teacher after casting his first spell and likewise passed it to Jodah after Jodah cast his first spell, a ball of light.

When Jodah later was led to Ith's prison by the Rag Man, he saw that Ith had been driven insane. After Ith went into a murderous rampage that resulted in the death of Mairsil and the destruction of the Conclave of Mages, Jodah managed to use the mirror to make him come to his senses.

Because the Fountain of Youth Jodah bathed in had dramatically slowed his aging, he remained practically unchanged through the following years while those around him died. The grief and despair that this caused made him descend into madness. To retain his sanity, he began to store his memories in the mirror. After wiping his memory clean, he restored it from the mirror, drained of its emotional attachment. He lived so long that he was granted the title of Archmage Eternal and oversaw the City of Shadows as it changed into the School of the Unseen.

Kayla's Music Box is a legendary artifact on Dominaria from the time of the Brothers' War.

Kayla's Music Box is a small music box owned by Kayla bin-Kroog that was repaired by Urza. She questioned if he repaired it as a display of affection for her or just a display of skill. The box appears metallic with a lion head emblem on its front. When opened it has a mirror as the underside of the lid and several different shaped gears that presumably create the music.

entities.name: Keld
entities.description:
Keld is a warrior nation in the western and northern parts of Aerona's cold Icehaven subcontinent on Dominaria. The Keldons are known and feared as conquerors and mercenaries.

The people of Keld are human, but they are like no other humans anywhere. Nearly all adults stand over six feet tall, and seven feet is not uncommon. Keldons are remarkably resistant to the cold of their homeland. They are massively muscled and have gray skin (ranging from ashy gray-white to deeper blue-gray). Their hair points sharply down in the middle of the forehead and at either temple but recedes elsewhere. Keldons value self-reliance, strength, and courage. At best, they are proud, pragmatic, and passionate. At worst, they can be reckless, hot-tempered, and violent.

Though they are often perceived as a horde of brutish, unthinking barbarians, a threat to civilization in all its forms, they have a deep and rich culture that goes back many centuries. Having endured devastation on a massive scale and lived through their own prophesied apocalyptic judgment, today's Keldons ﬁght to be worthy of their glorious ancestors, their unforgiving home, and their strongest champions.

The warhost has long been the basic unit of Keldon society, consisting of anywhere from a few dozen Keldons to thousands. The warlords rule through strength and unity. By the power of Keldon's magic, each warhost's loyalty and zeal empower its warlord. The leader of Keld is the Grand Warlord. Before the Twilight, the warlords held the title of Doyen. Nowadays, the two roles are separated. In the more civilized areas of central Keld, doyens are appointed by the Grand Warlord to settle civic disputes, while the warhosts still choose their leaders. Overseers are appointed by the Grand Warlord as her liaisons to warhosts.

entities.name: Kelsinko
entities.description:
Kelsinko was a settlement deep within Fyndhorn on Terisiare during the Ice Age of Dominaria.

Kelsinko was located at the ruins of Citanul.

Kelsinko was home to both humans and elves. Citizens of the town were present when Freyalise cast her World Spell to end the Ice Age.

Like most of the rest of Fyndhorn, Kelsinko sank beneath the sea during the Flooding of Terisiare that followed the World Spell. Jaya Ballard led a team of mages to try to keep the waters of the sea at bay, but eventually failed. Refugees from Kelsinko headed west to Yavimaya, led by Kaysa and Jaeuhl Carthalion. Others fled northward, taking their druids with them. Jaya was one of the last ones out of the city, and she saw the first waves wash over Kelsinko's grand plaza and its murals peel away from the rising tides, as new creatures — fish, sea scorpions, and strange monsters wrapped in crab-shell armor - were taking over the sunken buildings.
entities.short_description: Kelsinko was a settlement deep within Fyndhorn on Terisiare during the Ice Age of Dominaria.

entities.name: Khone
entities.description:
Khone was a kingdom east of the Great Sulgh Salt Marsh in southeastern Corondor. It and Shikar were known as the Contrary Kingdoms.

Khone once was the name of an enchanted forest and the home of an ancient Force of Nature, until it was twisted into a swamp by Geyadrone Dihada and its spirit was bound to her service as Sol'Kanar the Swamp King. Kanar was an archaic term referring to the Kingdom of Khone. The term was replaced by Khonian. Restless and hungry, this kingdom has remained in isolation for far too long, and the Keeper of House Jet is a fickle lord.

Sol'Kanar destroyed the trade route between the Contrary Kingdoms, and forced the inhabitants to send slaves and goods on the Date of Tribute.

Since Khone's reconstruction, House Jet had but one guiding principle – don't get involved.

entities.name: Ki'pamu
entities.description:
Ki'pamu is the capital of the plane of Zhalfir.

Ki'pamu is the center of Zhalfir's government, military, and culture. The city is built at the edge of a vast lake and rivers that end in the Buleusi Bay and connect the city with Kiingal. The royal city had miles of stupendous walls and a deep-water harbor, with minarets, bazaars, labyrinthine streets, and communal wells. The palace of Zhalfir was made of marble, and was built throughout several generations, as one proud monarch after another enlarged and improved it until it settled in its final state during the Mirage Wars.

During the Mirage Wars Ki’pamu was a stronghold for Zhalfirin resistance against Kaervek and withstood attacks by Jolrael’s dragons. Here the prophet Asmira, Rashida Scalebane, Sidar Jabari and Hakim Loreweaver met to start the rescue of Mangara.

The alliance of Jamuraan city-states under the leadership of Ki'pamu was called the Ki'pamu League. Although located on the far side of the continent, the League appears to be part of Zhalfir's sphere of influence. This alliance against the Keldon invasion included:
entities.short_description: Ki'pamu is the capital of the plane of Zhalfir.

entities.name: Kiingal
entities.description:
The northernmost bastion of Zhalfirin rule, Kiingal was a large port located at the northern coast between Zhalfir and the Kukemssa Sea on Dominaria. It was connected to the capital Ki'pamu by a south-running river.

Kiingal was phased out alongside the rest of north-western Jamuraa since the planeswalker Teferi wanted to spare it from the horrors of the Phyrexian Invasion. It was forever lost from Dominaria after Jeska destroyed the time rift over the Zhalfirin Void.

When Teferi's spirit was shunted to Zhalfir after the Temporal Anchor malfunctioned, he traveled to Kiingal, eventually settling in a satellite village 12 miles to its east as its Shaper Guildmage. The satellite village is composed of clay-brick homes and long, low community buildings with living roofs. Holding granaries, kilns, smokehouses, cold forges, tanneries, and public stables, it is a hub for the farmers, fishers, hunters, and foragers that live in the region. Its creedhall, a small, domed temple, is the only building that stands out from the rest. A screen separates the inner domed space from the entryway, diming any light and muffling any sound that filters in from outside. The room under the dome is a pentagon, each face representing one of the five colors of magic. The mana well at its center holds a shallow, broad, stone bowl that burns Zhalfirin wellwood for incense. A low bench rings the room. Opposite the entry is a dark wall with a simple door set into it leading to humble quarters kept ready for members of the creeds.

At the conclusion of New Phyrexia's Invasion of the Multiverse, Wrenn and Realmbreaker returned the phased out Zhalfir to the multiverse by switching the landmass' place with that of New Phyrexia. Kiingal now exist as part of the plane of Zhalfir under the skies of Mirrodin.
entities.short_description: The northernmost bastion of Zhalfirin rule, Kiingal was a large port located at the northern coast between Zhalfir and the Kukemssa Sea on Dominaria. It was connected to the capital Ki'pamu by a south-running river.

entities.name: Koilos
entities.description:
Koilos is a mountainous location deep in the mountains of New Argive, part of the Terisian Isles on the plane of Dominaria. It borders the Western Desert and lies at the connection point of the Sardian Mountains and the Kher Ridges.

Koilos played an important part in the story of the Thran, the Brothers' War, and the Phyrexian Invasion of Dominaria.

During the time of the Thran Empire, the caves of Koilos were known as the Caves of the Damned and were inhabited by the Untouchables. These people were sick with Phthisis due to too much exposure to powerstones through working in the Mana Rig.

In these caves the planeswalker Dyfed built a permanent portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia. The planar portal could be closed by placing the two halves of the powerstone used to create it onto a pedestal in the caves. At the end of the Thran Civil War Yawgmoth ushered the last survivors into the portal to populate Phyrexia.

entities.description:
Korlis is an island in the archipelago of the Terisian Isles of Dominaria.

The island of Korlis is a fertile land, able to sustain the cultivation of burgundy wine grapes.

Korlis used to be part of the mainland. It was settled by seafarers from east of Terisiare. During the Brothers' War, Korlis was the southeastern of the three ancient coastal kingdoms of Terisiare.

Korlis was ruled by a merchant council and engaged primarily in trade with the rest of the nations of Terisiare. The kingdom used a currency called "korls."

entities.description: Kristina's Woods was a forest in Casindral on Dominaria's continet of Corondor where Kristina of the Woods took refuge. Home to the alliance that would defend the land against Ravidel's growing shadow. A Haven to all, this enchanted forest was declared open to all who would resist the conquerors of Corondor.

entities.name: Krosa
entities.description:
Krosa is a forest region on the continent Otaria on Dominaria. It is located between Tamingazin and Pardia. Krosa is the primary location for the Odyssey and Onslaught blocks.

Krosa is home to various species of large animals, as well as to centaur, nantuko and human druids. It is also famous for giant dragonflies and grendelkin. Krosa is unusual for a Dominarian forest, as it does not seem to feature any elves, which only live in the southern forests of the continent. Notable natives of Krosa included Seton, Stonebrow and Thriss; Kamahl eventually took residence in it too.

In the century following the Phyrexian Invasion of Dominaria, the forest’s size and density significantly increased. Hunting dropped off due to the suddenly increased ferocity of Krosan wildlife, giant thorns began springing up in the middle of paths, trees moved to block travel, and nantuko presence in the forest increased. The once-friendly druids who inhabited the forest grew somber and suspicious, while Krosan centaurs, already unfriendly people, became vigilant to the point of paranoia.

Krosa was a frequent target of Cabal poachers, who would capture fierce animals from the forest and bring them back to the pits to fight as entertainment for the crowds. Its foundations were corrupted by the Cabal Patriarch.

entities.name: Lat-Nam Straits
entities.description:
The Lat-Nam Straits is a body of water in western Terisian Isles.

The Lat-Nam Straits are the stretches of the sea that separate Lat-Nam and the Halquina Islands from Almaaz and Gulmany. The straits between the islands range from wide to fairly narrow and allow for a wide combination of possible routes. The straits connect to the South Sea in the southeast, the Sea of Almaaz in the northeast, and the Ilesemare Sea in the north and west.

The Lat-Nam Straits followed the western shore of Terisiare before that continent was split into smaller islands. During the Brothers' War, the straits were narrower and dotted with more islands, bordering the Halquina Mountains and the Borderlands of Almaaz. During the Dark Age, the Straits grew even narrower with the cooling climate, with several of the smaller islands starting to join together. Smaller nations formed in the area at this time, including Jehesic and Iwset. During the Ice Age, the straits dried up completely, connecting Lat-Nam to the main continent. At the same time, the Great Glacier grew south and covered much of the area that had once belonged to the straits. Come the Flooding of Terisiare, the glaciers retreated and sea levels rose again, filling the straits with water once more.

entities.name: Leather Street
entities.description:
Leather Street is a part of Ki'pamu, the capital of Zhalfir, that is lined with ramshackle cottages, and roamed by beggars and thieves.

In the time before Mangara's Harmony, the Civic Guildmage Sabul Hajeen bid the angel Kotara seek out and kill Yirtag Ilmiera on Leather Street, to avenge the death of his brother.

The Legend of Jedit Ojanen is a Magic: The Gathering comic which was released in two volumes, in March–April 1996, by ARMADA.

The Legend of Jedit Ojanen, based on the card Jedit Ojanen, is no longer canon. The later novels of the Legends Cycle I provide a contradictory account of the same story.

Jedit Ojanen encounters other creatures seen on Magic cards. He spots a Fire Drake and gets a Healing Salve from passing Desert Nomads. At the cliffhanger climax on the last page of the issue, he encounters Johan.

entities.name: Living Armor
entities.description:
The Living Armor was a set of crafted armor that was able to self-animate, changing both form and texture to fit its intended wearer.

The sorceress Sacumon found the Living Armor in an armory beneath the Colekgan Mountains, although Vervamon later assumed it originated in Lat-Nam, and was brought to the mountains by the Niroso. Sacumon later offered the Living Armor to Yunnie, who initially declined it, as it appeared in the form of a small leather breastplate. However, when the blood witch coerced Yunnie to put it on, the leather straps fastened themselves and the armor molded itself to perfectly fit his broad, muscular chest. It pulsed with power, transmitting some of it to its wearer, instilling bravery and strength.

Using the armor, Yunnie became almost invincible, swinging the war against the elves of Eln Forest in favor of the Urhaalan Valley minotaurs, who had adopted Yunnie into their clan. However, the Living Armor also took a toll on its boon. Each battle where the armor granted Yunnie great strength, protection, and a sense of invulnerability, left him severely exhausted and drained afterward. After several battles, Yunnie noted that the armor became harder to remove and that the weakening effect was getting progressively stronger. He made several attempts at discarding the armor, but it would find ways to return to him and reattach itself. It also started deflecting blows off itself and onto its wearer, showing its inherently dangerous essence. Yunnie eventually did manage to tear the armor away from his body, removing several strips of skin and flesh along with it. The armor was then picked up by Yunnie's blood-brother, the minotaur Mytaru, to defeat the stone colossus Tiyint. Mytaru actively used the rebound effect of the armor to make the giant statue's crushing grip cause its imbued magic to weaken, rendering the statue lifeless at last, although at the cost of Mytaru's life.

The shapeshifter Isak Glen'Dard, having witnessed the battle and the deaths of Mytaru and Tiyint, then claimed the Living Armor for himself, donning it underneath his clothes so that it would remain a secret advantage for him.
entities.short_description: The Living Armor was a set of crafted armor that was able to self-animate, changing both form and texture to fit its intended wearer.

entities.name: Long-daggers
entities.description:
The Long-daggers were two magical knives kept by Grenfell Mor that have the power, when activated together, to destroy the Golgothian Sylex with a spell.

Jared Carthalion and Kristina of the Woods retrieved the two long-daggers from the Golthonor Sea and Telemar City. Jared used them at the Dueling Chasm of Golthonor to deactivate the Golgothian Sylex and then seemingly destroyed it with a shatter spell.

entities.name: Love Song of Night and Day
entities.description:
The Love Song of Night and Day is a poem from Jamuraa, Dominaria. It tells the story of the love between night and day, and their separation. It was written by Jenny Scott, a long-time editor at Wizards of the Coast and frequent contributor to The Duelist magazine, who wrote it as part of the worldbuilding for Jamuraa. It was told through flavor text of seventeen cards released in Mirage and Visions. Much later, the Song was referenced again in King of the Pride from Modern Horizons and Love Song of Night and Day in Dominaria United.

HE: Wrap yourself in your best bright clothes, your red and purple scarves of silk. Run with me to the festival, where we will dance until sunrise. The dwarves will beat their funny drums of zebra skins and hollowed trees, while stiltwalkers perform, and the musician blows his bamboo flute.

SHE: And late in the night, the poets and storytellers entertain, delight us with their dancing words, as we listen, clapping by the fire.

perhaps a hippopotamus if only you can catch it first.

entities.name: Mana Rig
entities.description:
The Mana Rig was a complex of structures built by the Thran on Dominaria's continent of Shiv.

Perched upon a cliff's edge in Shiv's brutal desert, the metal structure had the size and complexity of a small city. The huge installation was full of functional Thran technology. Its original purpose was to create huge crystal batteries of energy, called powerstones, that can be used to run all manner of artifact devices. It also could produce Thran metal, a nearly indestructible kind of steel. At the time of the Thran, there had been more than one Mana Rig, another being located at Halcyon in Terisiare.

Originally built by the Thran as a prototype powerstone factory, the Mana Rig was found by Urza during the events of Urza's Legacy. As a sacred location to the Shivans, Urza's entry into the Rig nearly sparked a war. He managed to get the Goblins and Viashino to work together to operate the Rig, which proved necessary as the Thran had built sections of it with goblin workers in mind. It produced Thran metal for the Skyship Weatherlight as well as a powerstone in which the mana from Serra's Realm would later be stored.

During the Phyrexian Invasion of Dominaria, the Mana Rig came under attack by Phyrexian forces who came to either claim it or, failing that, destroy it. However, to both Yawgmoth's minions and Urza's surprise, the seemingly defenseless structure launched a counterattack by deploying a detachable and mobile segment of itself that could shoot huge geysers of molten lava with deadly accuracy, a feature installed by Jhoira who had been in charge of the complex.
entities.short_description: The Mana Rig was a complex of structures built by the Thran on Dominaria's continent of Shiv.

entities.name: Mightstone
entities.description:
The Mightstone was half of a Thran powerstone that played a major part in the Brothers' War on Dominaria. Its counterpart was the Weakstone.

The Mightstone was an ancient Thran crystal capable of empowering artifacts. It was created when Dyfed cracked a large powerstone in half to establish a permanent portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia. Afterward, Yawgmoth secretly placed the two halves (the Mightstone and the Weakstone) inside Glacian to worsen his case of phthisis. While inside him, the two halves absorbed Glacian's essence, empowering them with his knowledge of artifice. After Glacian's death, his wife Rebbec discovered Yawgmoth's evil nature and combined the two halves to close the portal Dyfed had created, sealing him in Phyrexia.

Following the destruction of Halcyon in the Thran Civil War, the two stones remained in the Caves of Koilos for approximately 5000 years, until the ruins of the Thran capital were excavated by Tocasia and her two apprentices, the brothers Urza and Mishra. As they excavated the Hall of Tagsin, the two brothers uncovered the pedestal where the two stones were kept together. Urza took the Mightstone and Mishra the Weakstone, unwittingly reactivating the gate to Phyrexia. They also accidentally awoke the su-chi that guarded the vault, who then promptly attacked the brothers and their master. Urza tried to use his stone to stop them but found that he had only made them stronger, the creatures only being stopped when Mishra used his stone against them.

As the excavation work wore on, the brothers became increasingly jealous of each other, each wanting to possess the other's stone. This came to a head back in the encampment, where they argued and became violent, using the stones against each other before accidentally killing Tocasia when she tried to calm them. After their master's death, the two brothers separated and over the years began building armies and claiming territories. The Mightstone was directly involved at the beginning of the Brothers' War when Mishra slept with Urza's wife Kayla and had her bring him the Mightstone. Urza discovered them and reclaimed the powerstone, declaring war on his brother. During this war, Urza retained possession of the Mightstone, using it to bolster his legions.

entities.name: Minorad
entities.description:
Minorad was an independent city-state in the northeast of the Dominarian continent of Corondor.

The Valley of Minorad was the northernmost civil part of the continent, situated between the Urlan Wilds and the Northern Wilds and north of Kristina's Woods. It was a refuge for survivors after the Ice Age and the breaking up of Terisiare, later becoming a center of learning.

The Library of Minorad was the crown of the city of Minorad, and the center of knowledge for its Sages.

In the year 1 (according to the sages of Minorad), inspired by the teachings of Taysir of Rabiah, there was a summit of mages and planeswalkers who swore to protect the world and its inhabitants. Participants were: Ash Warlord Embereck, Liana of Minorad, Kristina of the Woods, Altair of Coloni, and Grenfell Mor of Golthonor. The Summit was disturbed by the battlemage Ravidel, who threatened to destroy the world with the Golgothian Sylex if they interfered in his plans. As the leader Kristina surrendered, Embereck immediately left. After the mages promised not to interfere with Ravidel, they were banned from Minorad, so that the city could go on undisturbed for almost 1300 years. 1276 years later, Ravidel broke his promise: he returned and destroyed the city and western Corondor in search of the moxen, which would help him to recall his master, Taysir.

entities.name: Mirari
entities.description:
The Mirari was an artifact of unspeakable power that appeared on Otaria roughly a century after the Phyrexian Invasion.

The word “mirari” was an ancient word for a fantastic wish-granting artifact and the Mirari certainly matched that description, tapping into its wielder's desires and making them real. However, the Mirari also inevitably caused disaster to strike the bearer, usually leading to their death. Another effect it had was that it caused intense longing in those that saw it, causing many individuals to become obsessed with owning it. It initiated a devastating cycle of warfare and magical disasters across Otaria before it was retrieved by its creator, Karn, who had only intended for it to be a probe. He took it to his artificial plane, Argentum, where he used it as the core of the golem he created as the plane's guardian, Memnarch.

The Mirari was found by Chainer in an old mansion, where it called to the young cabalist with promises of power. However, Chainer instead decided it was only fit for the Cabal's leader to own and so presented it as a gift to the First, who put it in the Cabal's coffers as a prize in the upcoming three-day tournament. It was there that Kamahl first saw the Mirari and became obsessed with it. However, it was instead claimed by Lieutenant Kirtar of the Order as a reward for his role in defending Cabal City from a dragon attack. Kirtar took the artifact with the intention of destroying it, but it soon corrupted him with promises of glory. Instead, he took it to the Order's citadel and used it to kill Pianna, the human leader of the Order on Otaria. However, Kirtar was unable to end his spell, which went on to devastate the citadel and kill the Lieutenant.

The Mirari itself was recovered by Laquatus's minion Turg. The merman had been pursuing the artifact ever since Kirtar had claimed it and seized his chance to get hold of it. However, Laquatus's plan was frustrated when Turg gave the Mirari to Captain Satas, who then took it to Emperor Aboshan. Laquatus raced to recover it, but found that it had been lost within the royal treasure vaults. In order to get his hands on it, Laquatus made a deal with the cabalists that had been brought in to index the vaults: he would let them keep whatever valuable artifacts they wanted in exchange for giving him the Mirari when they found it. However, the Mirari was found first by the emperor himself.
entities.short_description: The Mirari was an artifact of unspeakable power that appeared on Otaria roughly a century after the Phyrexian Invasion.

entities.name: Mirari Saga
entities.description:
The Mirari Saga is the set of storylines that took place in the aftermath of the Weatherlight Saga. Not one continuous story per se, the Mirari Saga tells of the devastation wrought by a powerful artifact, the Mirari, created as a probe by Karn and sent to Dominaria, where it caused massive havoc on the continent of Otaria during the Odyssey and Onslaught blocks.

Afterward, Karn retrieved the artifact and took it to his artificial plane, granting the Mirari sentience as Memnarch and putting it in charge, which led to the storyline of the Mirrodin block.

The disjointed storytelling of this era is a result of the changing philosophy of Wizards of the Coast's continuity department. Wizards of the Coast considered the multi-year epic style of the Weatherlight Saga to be a failure; the Mirari Saga was but slow transitional period between that model of storytelling and the current, setting-based philosophy.

entities.name: Mishra's Fortress
entities.description:
Mishra's Fortress was the base Mishra built after the Fall of Kroog.

Mishra selected a site on the northwest tip of the Kher Ridges with a dominating view of the arid lands to the west - the Great Desert. Through a trick of the weather patterns, this area was well-watered and was swathed in trees so large that they might have been planted by the Thran themselves. They were some type of oak, with thick, heavy trunks and long, horizontal branches. Some of the quarters and laboratories were nestled among those branches. Surrounding the grove of great trees, most of the smaller timbers downslope had been cleared. Part of the clearing was for cultivation, but more of it was for smaller foundries and forges. The residue of those forges spilled slag, the unusable remains of their industry, down the slopes and into the streams at the foot of the hills.

One of the great trees had died eons ago, leaving a massive stump over sixty feet high and twice that in diameter. Mishra had the stump hollowed out and converted into his private workshop to rival the crushed ornery in now-dead Kroog. The workshop towered over visitors, the windows carved through its outer bark lit by fires within. The windows were oddly shaped, formed more by the twists of the once-living bark than by Mishra's own needs. They looked like malignant, winking eyes. The workshop proper was two parts library, two parts workshop, and two parts throne room. A great dark oak throne had been pushed against a wall, piled high with pillows and resting on a purple carpet, pulled from the wreckage of the palace of Kroog.

A few years later, during the siege of Sarinth, Gix was brought by the Brotherhood of Gix to the fortress while Mishra was planning to relocate his headquarters to Tomakul. At that point, the great trees that had originally cradled the factories were dead, their lumber sawn up and used to make catapults, rams, dragon engines, and other war machines. The surviving stumps had been hollowed out and converted to barracks and foundries and plated with sheets of thin copper. There were still humans about, both warriors and slaves, but much of the work was now done by automatons - great clanking beasts that shuffled mindlessly from one task to the next. Gix found that he could not murder Mishra and steal the Weakstone, as the stone defended both itself and its master. Instead, Gix decided to corrupt Mishra and bring him over to the side of Phyrexia.
entities.short_description: Mishra's Fortress was the base Mishra built after the Fall of Kroog.
